title: AA-EU Coins
summary: An auction / e-commerce platform I am developing myself.
problem: I needed my own trading platform: the full path from idea to a product running on a server — not a training project on localhost.
solution: An auction / e-commerce platform built with intensive use of AI at every stage — from planning and code to debugging and server deployment.
architecture: DEPLOYMENT — running on a real server
verifiedByOwner: The platform working on a real server
The full path idea → server → product
result: The platform runs on a server (aa-eucoins.de) and keeps evolving.
lessons: A product exists not when the code is finished, but when it is deployed and works for users.

title: CryptoGemScanner
summary: My own bot and service analyzing the crypto market in real time via API.
problem: Crypto market data changes constantly — tracking signals by hand is impossible, so an automated pipeline from data to publication is required.
solution: The system connects to market APIs, analyzes data in real time, generates signals and automatically publishes them on the website and in a Telegram channel.
aiHelpedWith: Designing the API → analyze → signal → publish pipeline
verifiedByOwner: Stable signal generation from real API data
Automatic publication on the site and in Telegram
result: The service is live: cryptogemscanner.com + a Telegram channel.
lessons: Reliable automation is mostly about handling external API failures, not just the happy path.

title: Windows: accounting / products
summary: A desktop Windows application for managing products, prices, sales, expenses and operational data.
problem: A real workflow needed its own accounting tool: products, prices, sales history, purchases, expenses and fast operational work with data.
solution: A desktop application built for a real need: products, prices, sales history, purchases, expenses, data import/export and fast operational handling.
verifiedByOwner: The application is used daily in my own workflow
result: A working tool in daily use.
lessons: The best test of an application is your own daily work in it, not a demo scenario.

title: Windows: links + reminders
summary: A second desktop Windows utility: daily work with links, information organization and reminders.
problem: Daily work with many links and information did not fit standard tools — a fast own prototype was needed.
solution: A second desktop application for Windows supporting daily work: links, information organization, reminders.
verifiedByOwner: Used in my own daily workflow
lessons: A second project on the same stack goes faster — you reuse experience, not only code.

title: SEO — practice
summary: Building sites and configuring SEO on my own with AI, verifying results on real search phrases.
problem: A site without search traffic does not work: I needed to understand SEO in practice, not from articles.
solution: I built sites myself and configured SEO with AI: keyword research, content optimization, positioning. I checked the effects on real phrases in search.
architecture: CHECK — verifying positions on real phrases
verifiedByOwner: Positions for real phrases in search
result: SEO understanding verified in practice: AI → WWW → SEO → result.
lessons: SEO advice from articles and real search behavior are different things; only practice verifies.

title: GitHub — open code
summary: Repositories and projects showing practical use of JavaScript, React and AI-assisted coding.
problem: A skill has to be verifiable: the code is open, it can be read and run.
solution: Repositories and projects demonstrating practical JavaScript, React, AI-assisted coding and my own technical experiments.
verifiedByOwner: Code goes through test and iteration before publication
lessons: Public code disciplines you: you cannot just talk about it, you have to show it.
